whatItIs.text: A bulb of the Allium family whose pungency comes from sulfur compounds released only when the cells are crushed or chopped — the hotter and sharper the garlic, the more it was damaged.

historyNote.text: Native to Central Asia and northeastern Iran, garlic has been used for thousands of years by Babylonians, Egyptians, Romans, and Chinese alike; China today grows about 73% of the world's supply.

howToChoose.text: Choose heads that feel firm and heavy with tight, unbroken skin and no green sprouts; soft or sprouting bulbs have started using up their own flavour.

storage.text: Keep whole heads in a cool, dry, airy spot out of the sun; peeled cloves refrigerate in a sealed jar.

useItUp.text: Whole heads become sweet roasted paste, and peeled cloves freeze in oil cubes.

substitutions.note: gentler, sweeter; less heat, more subtlety
for rubs and dressings; no bite, so add with salt early
